artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{M_k\}_{k=0}^\infty$ be a sequence of positive numbers satisfying $M_0 = 1$ and the log-convexity-type condition
$$\frac{M_{k+j}}{M_k M_j} \ge \binom{k+j}{j} \quad\text{for all } k, j \ge 0,$$
together with the non-quasianalyticity condition
$$\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{M_k}{M_{k+1}} < \infty.$$
Let $X \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a compact set. Consider the class $A(X)$ of functions $f$ on $X$ that are limits, in the norm
$$\|g\| = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{1}{M_k}\,\sup_{X} |g^{(k)}|,$$
of rational functions with poles off $X$. Then $A(X)$ is a commutative Banach algebra under this norm.

Question: Is the maximal ideal space of $A(X)$ equal to $X$ (with the natural identification of points of $X$ with evaluation characters)?

It is known that the answer is affirmative when $X$ is the closed unit disc or a compact interval of the real line. The problem asks whether this holds for an arbitrary compact set $X \subset \mathbb{C}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return results that confirm a resolution of this maximal-ideal-space question for the non-quasianalytic Banach algebra of rational approximants on a general compact subset of the complex plane. No published proof or counterexample for arbitrary compact $X$ was located, so the current status is unknown to this search.
